//: Per-school configuration boundary (proposal §7.3). Copy to appsettings.School.json per deployment; never commit a real school's file or secrets. In containers these values arrive via environment variables from the compose .env instead.

School.Name: Example Synthetic College
School.//BrandColour: Optional school brand colour, #rrggbb or #rgb (ADR-0040 §3). Omit it and the neutral default palette is used. The API refuses to start on a value it cannot parse, or one that reaches 4.5:1 against neither black nor white. FIRST-RUN SEED ONLY — after the first start the brand colour is edited in the app (ADR-0045).
School.//HouseColours: Optional per-house colour, #rrggbb or #rgb (ADR-0044 §2), keyed by the house code from Houses (matched case-insensitively). Omit the block, or any house, and that house renders text-only. A value that cannot be parsed, or that repeats another house's colour, is dropped to text-only with a startup warning — it never stops the API. Env form: School__HouseColours__BANKSIA. FIRST-RUN SEED ONLY — after the first start houses and their colours are edited in the app (ADR-0045).

Imports.//: Path to the roster import mapping (see config/import-mapping.example.json). Per-deployment file, mounted read-only in containers.

AzureAd.//: PROVIDER 1 (default): Entra ID cloud, Microsoft.Identity.Web confidential web app (ADR-0001/0007). Every tenant-specific value lives here or in env vars (AzureAd__TenantId etc.) — never in code. ClientSecret arrives via environment/secret store (AzureAd__ClientSecret), never in this file. With hybrid AD → Entra sync, on-prem AD stays the source of truth.

Adfs.//: PROVIDER 2 (alternative): on-prem ADFS 2019+ or any generic OIDC provider, via the standard OpenID Connect handler (ADR-0007). Use for schools that authenticate through ADFS (externally reachable via a Web Application Proxy so off-network venue devices can sign in). Selected when Identity:Provider='Adfs', or inferred when AzureAd is absent and Authority+ClientId are set here. Leave blank/remove this whole section on Entra deployments. ClientSecret via env (Adfs__ClientSecret).
Adfs.//NameClaimType: Optional: the token claim to use as the display name (ADFS often 'upn').

Identity.//Provider: Optional explicit auth provider: 'Entra', 'Adfs', or 'DevAuth'. Omit to infer from which of AzureAd/Adfs is populated (falls back to DevAuth).

DevAuth.//: Development-only header auth fallback (X-Dev-Subject / X-Dev-Roles). MUST remain false in any school deployment.

Identity.//GroupsClaimType: Token claim carrying group memberships. Entra uses 'groups' (default, object ids). ADFS emits whatever your relying-party claim rule sends (e.g. 'group' with AD group NAMES) — set this to match, then map its values in GroupToRoleMappings below.
Identity.//GroupToRoleMappings: Group identifier -> platform role (proposal §8, ADR-0016). Entra: security-group OBJECT IDs. ADFS: whatever the group claim carries (typically AD group names). Mapped at request time, provider-agnostically. Every entry in the block below is a real mapping — do NOT add '//' comment keys inside it, they bind as a group whose role fails to parse and logs a warning per request.
Identity.//GroupToRoleMappings-FourRoles: SIX GROUPS, FOUR ROLES (ADR-0016). The groups do not change — the tenant is untouched — but three of them now map to the SAME role: EVENT_ADMINS, VERIFIERS and RECORDS all resolve to CarnivalAdministrator. That collapse IS the change. OFFICIALS -> Recorder, VIEWERS -> Viewer, SYSADMIN -> SystemAdministrator (unchanged, and it holds every carnival policy as well as imports so a school with one technical person is never locked out). Someone in two collapsed groups gets ONE CarnivalAdministrator claim, so their audit ActorRole shortens accordingly; audit history is never rewritten and keeps the old names.
Identity.//GroupToRoleMappings-Aliases: TEMPORARY: the six retired names (EventAdministrator, Verifier, RecordsManager -> CarnivalAdministrator; ResultsOfficial -> Recorder; ReadOnlyViewer -> Viewer) still resolve, as aliases, so a code deploy and this config edit may land in either order. An alias hit logs at Information — that log line is the removal condition. The aliases are removed once each deployment's mapping names the four roles below and /me confirms it (ADR-0016 §4). Deploy ordering is code first, config second: new role names in front of an old server is the one state the aliases cannot rescue.
